_comment_family: The name Windows knows this file by, which is also the one the
@font-face registration below hands the canvas. The file's own
typographic family is 'Gilroy' with 'ExtraBold' as the subfamily;
asking for 'Gilroy' alone would let any other cut of the family
installed on the machine answer, and a title laid out against a
Regular is a title laid out against the wrong metrics.
ExtraBold is the weight the folder holds. It is the heaviest cut
shipped here and the one the channel is set in — if a true Bold is
ever added, it arrives as its own face pack rather than as a change
to this one, so the two cannot be confused for each other.
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css: this face arrived with a channel and is
registered from this JSON, which is the route content/README.md
describes. Nothing has to be added to the stylesheet for it.
_comment_local: What the machine may already know the face by, tried after the file.
The first is the Windows full name (name ID 4) and is also what the
installer registers the face under; the second is the family Windows
lists it in, which is what a browser matches a local() by name.
Unlike scale-condensed-bold, this name is the font's own rather than
one this app invented, so a machine answering to it is answering with
this face — which is exactly what the fallback route is for.
